description_full: KOSE Holdings Corporation manufactures and sells cosmetics in Japan and internationally. The company operates through two segments, Cosmetics Business and Cosmetology Business. It offers cosmetics under the Sekkisei, Esprique, and One By Kosé brands through cosmetics stores, mass merchandisers, and drugstores; and cosmetics and toiletries, such as shampoos and conditioners through mass retailers, drugstores, department stores, convenience stores, and other retail outlets, as well as skin diagnosis services. The company was formerly known as KOSÉ Corporation and changed its name to KOSE Holdings Corporation in January 2026. KOSE Holdings Corporation was founded in 1946 and is headquartered in Tokyo, Japan.

financial_summary: Kose Corp. is a small-cap consumer defensive business with a $1.9B market cap on $2.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -0% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.
Returns on capital run at 7% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 70% confirm genuine pricing power.
The company is burning through $65M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 2.7% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 36% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
